title: Schur-ladder identity badSet=-{(k+1)-subset sums}, descending one dyadic level via the squaring fold: the identity + esymm2_inflate descent are TRUE and proven, but the recursion welds to the depth-collapse wall (capacity-only)
wall: W depth-collapse / W-BGK-Paley. The Schur-ladder recursion C050 chains is the dyadic squaring tower, and pinning the first t symmetric functions via the descent costs r_levels = ceil(log2(t+1)) squaring steps, each of which HALVES the usable transversal (orbit size 2^r). At a window-interior radius the agreement gap is t ~ r = (1-delta)*n = Theta(n), so r_levels ~ log2(n) and the transversal collapses to n/2^{r_levels} = O(1): the concentrated bad set the descent certifies degrades from super-poly (near capacity, constant t) to O(1)/linear-in-cosets (deep interior). This is EXACTLY the already-logged DISPROOF_LOG depth-collapse wall: O23/Round-8 (the order-4/2^r omega-closure depth-collapse paragraph) and O25/Round-9 CosetWallDeepInteriorNoGo.lean (super-poly count provably -> linear past delta=1-2rho). The residual worst-case spread one level down is the same open subgroup subset-sum / BGK-Paley core.
evidence: Exact-integer probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C050_schur_ladder_descent.py (DP over (subset-size, residue mod q) bitmask, exact, no sampling) on PROPER dyadic subgroups mu_n < F_q^* (NEVER full group): n=8 q=1009 (beta=3.33) & q=65537 (beta=5.33); n=16 q=7681 (3.23) & q=65537 (4.0); n=32 q=65537 (3.2) & q=786433=3*2^18+1 (3.92); n=64 q=786433 (3.26); all n=2^mu << sqrt q, q=1 mod n. (1) VERIFIED the F15->F3 identity: at the ladder stack the bad set = negated (k+1)-subset-sum image of mu_n; the probe reproduces the in-tree Lean number exactly -- (k+1)=3 at n=8 gives 40 distinct sums < C(8,3)=56, matching LadderSchurReduction.lean's docstring claim '40 = spectrum < 56'; small-k spreads stay sub-q and structured (n=16: 113/120 at k+1=2, 464/560 at k+1=3; n=32: 449/496, 3264/4960; n=64: 1985/2016, 39552/41664). (2) VERIFIED the F12 descent IS the dyadic squaring tower: squaring is exactly 2-to-1 on a 2-power subgroup, mu_n -> mu_{n/2} -> ... -> mu_1 (probe prints each level halving). (3) THE LOAD-BEARING TEST -- spread at WINDOW INTERIOR vs the descent: at rho in {1/2,1/4}, interior subset-size r=(1-delta)n = Theta(n) (r=10..39 across n=16..64), the top-level subset-sum spread SATURATES to the full field q (65537, 786433 -- i.e. EVERY scalar bad, the degenerate #400-trap full-field regime, not a structured counterexample), while the descent needs r_levels=ceil(log2(r+1)) = 4,5,6 steps which collapses the transversal to n/2^{r_levels} = 1 or 2 -> concentrated count C(1,.)<=2 or C(2,.)<=4, i.e. O(1). Contrast: near capacity (k+1=2,3) the spread is < q and structured. The collapse is sharp and monotone in n. Cross-checked against the in-tree proven Lean: LadderSchurReduction.lean (boundary_slice_ladder_badSet_eq, axiom-clean) and SubsetSumE2PairingInflate.lean (esymm2_inflate, twoSymmCount_ge_squareSubsetSum, axiom-clean) -- BOTH genuinely true; the descent residual is acknowledged open in SubsetSumE2PairingInflate.lean's own 'Honest scope' docstring ('reduces to the same open question one level down') and discharged-as-a-wall in DISPROOF_LOG O23/O25.
honest_note: NOT a closure and NOT a refutation of any Lean lemma -- both cited files are genuinely proven and axiom-clean. C050 is a CORRECT structural cartography: the Schur-ladder identity really does turn the ladder-stack bad set into the (k+1)-subset-sum set (F15->F3), and esymm2_inflate really does descend the t=2 joint (e1,e2) count to a t=1-shaped subset-sum count on the squares = mu_{n/2} (F12 one level down), with the dyadic squaring/FRI fold as the literal recursion. The probe confirms all three pieces exactly. What C050 does NOT do -- and its own attack_plan flags this ('measure whether the spread stays O(n) down the tower') -- is escape the depth-collapse wall: the descent pins the first t symmetric functions only by halving the free ground set per level, so reaching a deep window-interior gap (t~Theta(n)) forces ~log2(n) levels and collapses the transversal to O(1), yielding a linear/O(1) concentrated bad set, not the super-poly > q*eps* family the prize needs. At the interior the unstructured spread merely fills F_q (the degenerate trap). This is the SAME wall as DISPROOF_LOG O23/Round-8 depth-collapse and O25/Round-9 CosetWallDeepInteriorNoGo (super-poly -> linear past delta=1-2rho), and the residual square-subset-sum worst-case spread one level down is the open BGK/Paley subgroup subset-sum core. Verdict OPEN (welds back to an already-recorded wall); suitable as a one-line DISPROOF_LOG cross-reference noting C050's squaring-tower framing = the depth-collapse engine. Probe is exact integer (bitmask DP, no sampling) on 7 proper-subgroup primes; prize n=2^30 not directly enumerated (intractable) but the r_levels=log2(n) collapse is structural and matches the in-tree proven omega/coset wall theorems.
